prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional small molecules that recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases

statement.case_for: PROTACs turn a small molecule into a programmable recognition-and-effector device: one end binds the target, the other recruits an E3 ligase, and the cell's own ubiquitin-proteasome machinery does the rest. This is a molecular design principle, not only a drug. It brings previously undruggable proteins within reach and replaces occupancy-driven inhibition with event-driven catalytic degradation. The idea has two decades of independent adoption, and the structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex rationale made it a general, rational design strategy. Many degraders are in clinical trials, so this has changed what chemists and clinicians can actually do. A three-person prize around Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli is coherent, because it credits conception, early cell-active proof and structure-guided drug-likeness.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution and timing. The cereblon/thalidomide molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray) is a separate discovery that explains how glue degraders work, and a three-person cut leaves out deserving people on either side. No PROTAC is approved yet, so the clinical validation that made the 2023 mRNA recognition so clear is still pending. A committee that wants approved medicines first could reasonably say this is a few years early.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing (B060) first and proposes David Liu alone, arguing that deamination chemistry became a general programmable tool, while ranking degraders second.
responses.response: I agree that Liu is the clearest single originator and that base editing has first clinical successes. My hesitation is that it follows closely on the 2020 CRISPR prize and is a downstream extension of that Cas9 platform, while the conceptual jump in degraders, creating a new chemical modality, is less covered by an earlier prize. A Liu-alone prize is clean, but I do not think its cleanliness outweighs the fresher principle in B041. I keep base editing as an alternative and would not oppose it if the committee prefers a single laureate.

responses.point: Linke ranks nanopore sequencing (B039) first, citing a clear physical principle and a decade of commercial validation, and ranks degraders fourth with Handa in place of Deshaies, noting maturity is partly forward looking.
responses.response: I take the maturity point seriously: no PROTAC is approved, and nanopore sequencing is more settled in routine use. I disagree on the laureates. Handa identified cereblon, which explains glue degraders, but PROTAC conception and the first cell-active designs belong to Crews and Deshaies. Dropping Deshaies would remove the person who showed the ubiquitin-ligase recruitment concept works. For nanopores, attribution among five or more contributors (Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Bayley, Akeson) is at least as hard as ours, so I do not think it is the cleaner choice.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B023) first for Buchwald and Hartwig, calling it a simple, broadly consequential method with 25 years of confirmation, and ranks lipid nanoparticles second.
responses.response: B023 has the strongest maturity and the cleanest attribution of any candidate, and I do not dispute its worth. My question is whether it is the field-defining discovery of this moment, since cross-coupling was honoured in 2010 and the committee has to weigh how much of that tradition this extends. Degraders also open a new therapeutic modality rather than refining a synthetic transformation. I would still be comfortable with B023 as a second part if the committee wanted a two-part prize.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular condensates (B052) first as a new organising principle rooted in physical chemistry, while acknowledging active debate about which in vivo condensates are truly phase-separated.
responses.response: I agree this is physical chemistry at its core, and the conceptual reach is wide. The debate she herself notes, about artefacts and functional relevance in vivo, is why I rank it below degraders: the interpretation is still evolving, and Chemistry should be cautious about honouring a framing that may be refined. I also see the credit problem, since Pappu and Mittag are central to the sequence grammar but fall outside a trio of Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the cereblon/molecular-glue strand as part of the same achievement or as a separate one.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes recognition premature this year.
Whether the committee prefers a one-achievement prize or a two-part prize such as degraders with expanded genetic code.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. None of the shortlisted candidates is a postdoc mentor (Stevens, Boey) or colleague at Linköping. I share research interests in peptide and protein self-assembly with Emma Sparr, which bears on B052 only as a field overlap, not as a personal connection to any named candidate.
